facts.text: Jesus gave him a new name: Cephas, which means Peter, a stone.
He was fishing with his brother Andrew when Jesus called them.
He walked on the water toward Jesus.
He said to Jesus, “You are the Christ, the Son of the living God.”
He denied knowing Jesus three times, then wept bitterly.
Jesus asked him three times, “Do you love Me?” and told him, “Feed My sheep.”
He was a disciple of John the Baptist and one of the first two to follow Jesus.
He found his brother Simon and brought him to Jesus.
He brought Jesus the boy with five barley loaves and two small fish.

james.family: Son of Zebedee, brother of John

facts.text: He was mending nets with his father Zebedee and his brother John when Jesus called him.
Jesus named James and John “Sons of Thunder.”
He saw Jesus raise Jairus' daughter.
He was with Jesus on the mountain at the Transfiguration.
He was the first of the Twelve to die for Jesus.

john.family: Son of Zebedee, brother of James

facts.text: He was mending nets with his father and brother when Jesus called him.
He was with Jesus on the mountain at the Transfiguration.
Jesus sent him and Peter to prepare the Passover meal.

john.tradition: Christians have long believed John is “the disciple whom Jesus loved” in John's Gospel, and that he wrote it. The Gospel itself does not name him.

facts.text: Jesus found him and said, “Follow Me.”
He told Nathanael, “Come and see.”
Jesus asked him where they could buy bread for the crowd.
He asked Jesus, “Lord, show us the Father.”
Jesus saw him under the fig tree before Philip called him.
He said, “You are the Son of God! You are the King of Israel!”

nathanael.tradition: The lists of the Twelve name Bartholomew next to Philip, and John's Gospel names Nathanael with Philip. Many Christians believe they are the same man, but the Bible does not say so directly.

facts.text: He is named in the lists of the Twelve.
He said, “Let us also go, so that we may die with Him.”
He asked Jesus, “How can we know the way?”
When he saw the risen Jesus, he said, “My Lord and my God!”

matthew.hometown: Capernaum, where his tax booth was

facts.text: Jesus saw him at the tax booth and said, “Follow Me.”
He held a great banquet for Jesus at his house.

matthew.tradition: Christians have long believed Matthew wrote the Gospel that carries his name.

facts.text: He is named in every list of the Twelve. The Bible tells us little else about him.

thaddaeus.alsoCalled: Judas son of James (not Judas Iscariot)

facts.text: Matthew and Mark call him Thaddaeus; Luke calls him Judas son of James.
At the Last Supper he asked Jesus why He would show Himself to them and not to the world.
He is called Simon the Zealot. The Bible tells us little else about him.
He was chosen as one of the Twelve.
He kept the money bag and took from it.
He agreed to hand Jesus over for thirty pieces of silver.
When Jesus was condemned, Judas was filled with remorse and gave the silver back.
